pages.title: About Eric A. Hudson
pages.text: ABOUT THE EDITOR Eric A. Hudson Commercial trial lawyer. Constitutional advocate. THE LAWYER BEHIND THE TRACKER Eric A. Hudson Partner · Arambula Terrazas PLLC · Austin, Texas Eric Hudson is a litigation partner at Arambula Terrazas PLLC with nearly two decades of experience in commercial litigation, constitutional disputes, injunctions, and appeals. He represents clients in state and federal courts and arbitration, including matters involving religious institutions and governmental action. Before entering private practice, Eric served as a senior government litigator, handling complex constitutional, election, and public-law disputes. His practice combines trial advocacy with experience before the Texas Supreme Court, the Fifth Circuit, and the United States Supreme Court. Religious liberty work Eric represents individuals and institutions in disputes over the freedom to practice their faith and the right to equal treatment by government. His work includes challenges involving access to public education programs, land use, and state regulatory enforcement. Eric served as counsel of record for the Legal Insurrection Foundation in Mahmoud v. Taylor , a U.S. Supreme Court case about religious exercise in public schools. He filed an amicus brief in support of the petitioners . In coverage of an education case, Eric told The Texas Tribune and ProPublica , “Religious liberty is not a temporary pass issued after a lawsuit.” His work on disputes involving state investigations and land use has also been covered by KERA News and the Houston Chronicle . Texas Monthly’s October investigation examined the state’s securities case. Eric also represents the East Plano Islamic Center (EPIC) in its federal lawsuit against the Texas Funeral Service Commission, a case concerning the right to carry out religious funeral rites. KERA News covered the case in an article republished by Texas Public Radio . pages.title: Religious liberty: issues and sources
pages.text: THE ISSUES & THE SOURCES Religious liberty in Texas and the United States. A starting point for following religious freedom, constitutional rights, legislation, and the public debate. What this site follows Religious liberty questions reach beyond worship services. They arise in education, public benefits, professional licensing, employment, land use, and the treatment of religious institutions. Texas Religious Liberty Watch brings together official legislative records and daily news coverage to make those developments easier to follow. The focus extends across faiths. A proposed law affecting one religious community can raise questions relevant to others. The tracker identifies measures for closer examination; inclusion does not express support or opposition. Texas legislation and state law The bill tracker covers the 90th Regular Session of the Texas Legislature. It includes potentially relevant bills and proposed constitutional amendments, links to official text and history, and a personal watchlist. A filed proposal is not an enacted law. Review labels distinguish screened captions from reviewed text. For the underlying Texas legal sources, start with Texas Constitution article I, section 6 , and the Texas Religious Freedom Restoration Act, Civil Practice and Remedies Code chapter 110 . The official text is the source to consult when evaluating a particular provision. National developments The First Amendment addresses both the free exercise of religion and governmental establishment of religion. Federal litigation and national policy debates can affect how religious liberty questions arise in Texas. The National Archives’ Bill of Rights transcript provides the constitutional text. Our news watch gathers Texas and national headlines with publisher attribution and links to the coverage. Reporting, opinion, advocacy, proposed legislation, and court decisions are different kinds of sources. Read the underlying text and relevant decisions before drawing conclusions about legal effect. Follow an issue from source to discussion Find a proposal in the bill tracker and read its official text. Save it to your browser’s watchlist and add private working notes. Use the news watch to follow related reporting and public debate. Check the linked official record for current legislative action. EXPLORE THE SITE Keep the sources close. Add the Texas 90R Liberty Tracker to your home screen. Follow bills and keep a personal watchlist with one tap. Your legislative desk, on your phone. The app contains the 90R bill tracker and your personal watchlist. Use the app menu to open hearings, court rulings, and news on the website. Choose your phone below to add the app. No account or app-store purchase is needed. Install 90R app ↓ Open 90R tracker → iPhone instructions Android instructions 90R 2027 SESSION APPLE IPHONE & IPAD Add it with Safari. Open this page in Safari . Tap Share . On some versions, open the More menu first. Choose Add to Home Screen . Scroll through the actions if needed. If shown, turn on Open as Web App , then tap Add . Look for the maroon-and-gold 90R Watch icon on your home screen. ANDROID Add it with Chrome. Open this page in Chrome . If the Install 90R app button appears above, tap it and confirm. In Chrome, you can also open the menu and choose Install app or Add to Home screen . Menu wording varies by browser version. Open the link in your browser if you arrived through LinkedIn, Facebook, or another app. The same tracker. A simpler way to open it. Twice-daily bill checks The app checks for new bills at 7:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. Central time each day through May 31, 2027. Connect to the internet and refresh to load the latest published snapshot. The app does not need a separate subscription. Saved content when offline After an online visit finishes preparing the app, the saved tracker can open without a connection. A notice identifies saved content. Check its snapshot date; official bill records and hearing links need an internet connection. Your watchlist stays yours Saved bills and notes stay on your device. Browser and installed-app storage may differ, and they do not sync across phones. Use Sources → Download personal backup , then restore that backup in the app if you need to transfer them. Use the mobile website anytime Installation is optional. The full mobile website ↗ includes the tracker, hearings, court rulings, and news. This is an installable web app, distributed directly from this website. No Apple App Store, Google Play, or Galaxy Store listing is required. It does not send push notifications.
